title: New generic apiserver routes must feed both SetupConfig and AugmentWebServicesWithCustomRoutes
answers: Why does a new route work with curl but not appear in the OpenAPI spec?
Why is a route documented in the spec but returns 404/refuses when called?
How do I mount a new generic endpoint (like search, trash, list-keys) on the apiserver?
body: Invariant: any slice of route builders passed into the apiserver must feed BOTH builder.SetupConfig and builder.AugmentWebServicesWithCustomRoutes in pkg/services/apiserver/service.go:start. A route reaching only SetupConfig is documented in OpenAPI but never actually served; reaching only the augment call makes it served but absent from the generated spec. Gating a route builder behind a config bool (e.g. keysroutes.Build's enabled flag) makes the gate genuine only because both call sites consume the same slice: off means absent from both, not mounted-but-refusing.
applies: Any new cross-cutting route (search/trash/keys-style) mounted globally in the Grafana apiserver service.
says: Why does my new endpoint appear in docs but returns 404 when called?

search: Generic apiserver routes must feed both SetupConfig and AugmentWebServicesWithCustomRoutes in pkg/services/apiserver/service.go:start, enforced by having both sites consume the same route-builder slice (e.g., keysroutes.Build). Passing routes only to SetupConfig documents them in OpenAPI but doesn't serve them; only to AugmentWebServicesWithCustomRoutes serves them undocumented. Config-gated builders work correctly because the same gate applies to both call sites, making off-state truly absent from both, not mounted-and-refusing. Applies to cross-cutting routes like search, trash, and keys-style endpoints mounted globally in the Grafana apiserver.
